name: Learning Lock-Free Data Structures (CAS Me If You Can blog series)

mentions.name: Learning Lock-Free Data Structures (CAS Me If You Can blog series)
mentions.description: A three-part blog series on learning lock-free data structures. It walks through building a Treiber Stack first in Go and then in C++, diagnosing ABA and use-after-free issues in the C++ implementation, touching on hazard pointers, and finishing with a benchmark comparison between a mutex-based and a lock-free version of the stack. LLMs were used as a teaching aid to explain concepts and handle setup, without generating code.
mentions.problem: Learning lock-free data structures is difficult and can otherwise require reading dense and obscure books.
mentions.source_excerpt:
Learning Lock-Free Data Structures:

- https://parallelthoughts.xyz/2026/03/cas-me-if-you-can-part-1/

- https://parallelthoughts.xyz/2026/07/cas-me-if-you-can-part-3/

Mostly me exploring how to build a Treiber Stack (first in Go, then in C++) -> Figuring out ABA and Use-After-Free in the C++ implementation, and then touching a bit of Hazard Pointers, and ending with a benchmark comparison b/w a mutex and a lock-free version of the stack.
